blurb: Small German ratter with a shaggy mane and a famously monkey-like expression
description: The Affenpinscher is a small German toy dog of Pinscher type, 25–30 cm tall, with a harsh, wiry coat, a monkey-like face and a past as a stable ratter.
answer: The Affenpinscher is a small German toy dog of Pinscher type. It was once kept on farms and in stables to catch mice and rats and is now mostly a companion. It weighs about 4 to 6 kg, stands 25 to 30 cm, and is known for its rough coat and monkey-like expression.

body: The name comes from the German Affe, meaning ape or monkey; it is sometimes called the Monkey Terrier, although it is a Pinscher, not a terrier. Pinschers were traditionally kept as stable dogs and were capable ratters. In 1895 Ludwig Beckmann listed the Affenpinscher among five Pinscher varieties, and the American Kennel Club recognised it in 1936. It is rare in Germany, averaging just under 21 new registrations a year from 2010 to 2024.

The coat is harsh and wiry when properly maintained, shaggier over the head and shoulders where it forms a mane, and shorter over the back and hindquarters. Clipping makes it softer and fluffier. FCI and British Kennel Club standards require black, while the American Kennel Club also allows grey, silver, red, black and tan, and beige.
The source text gives little detail on temperament. Once a stable ratter, it is today commonly kept as a companion animal.

Sources give little specific detail on care. The wiry coat needs regular grooming to keep its harsh texture, and as a small dog its exercise needs are generally modest, though daily walks and play are usually recommended.

A UK study found a mean lifespan of 9.3 years for the breed, while other published figures put typical life expectancy at 12 to 15 years. Conditions reported in the breed include luxating patella, a possible predisposition to cataracts, secondary syringomyelia associated with Chiari malformation, and seasonal flank alopecia; evidence on hip dysplasia is mixed.

faq.q: Why is it called an Affenpinscher?
faq.a: Affe is German for ape or monkey, a reference to the dog's monkey-like expression. Pinscher refers to its breed type.
No. Despite the nickname Monkey Terrier, it is classed with the Pinschers and Schnauzers.

faq.q: How big does an Affenpinscher get?
faq.a: It generally weighs 4 to 6 kg and stands about 25 to 30 cm at the withers.

faq.q: What colours do Affenpinschers come in?
faq.a: FCI and UK standards accept only black. The American Kennel Club also allows grey, silver, red, black and tan, and beige.
